speaker: johan_vosloo
headline: A PRINCIPLE MATTERS ONLY IF PRACTICE SURVIVES IT.
deck: Rule-of-law language must be tested against what institutions actually permit, prevent, review and disclose.
quote: A constitutional promise is meaningful only when ordinary administration behaves as though the promise is binding.
facts: Limits must bind officials as well as citizens.
Review must exist before failure becomes scandal.

tests.label: MANDATE
tests.note: The legal source of power is visible.

tests.label: LIMIT
tests.note: Power has an explicit edge it may not cross.

tests.label: REVIEW
tests.note: A credible institution can inspect the decision.

tests.label: DISCLOSURE
tests.note: The result enters a public record.

takeaway: Institutional legitimacy is the distance between the principle on paper and the behaviour that survives contact with practice.
